encoding_decisions.decision: Vertices are a `Fintype`+`DecidableEq` type `V` with `2 ≤ Fintype.card V` playing the role of \(V=[d]\); labeled DAGs are `Causalean.DAG V` (reuse), with `DAG.parents`, `DAG.children`, `DAG.isRoot`, `DAG.topoOrder`, `DAG.descendants` supplying \(\operatorname{Pa}_G,\operatorname{Ch}_G\), sources, and reverse-topological recursion.
encoding_decisions.why: Causalean's DAG already carries decidable edges, parent/child finsets, a derived edge-consistent topological order, and an `ofAcyclic` constructor; rebuilding a DAG layer would duplicate the cluster substrate.

encoding_decisions.decision: Count vectors and multi-indices are the single type `V →₀ ℕ` (`Cell V`), carried with the discrete σ-algebra; \(|k|\) is `k.sum (fun _ m => m)`. The observational law is `P : MeasureTheory.Measure (Cell V)` with `IsProbabilityMeasure`, and \(p_x = P.real {x}\).
encoding_decisions.why: `V →₀ ℕ` is exactly `MvPowerSeries.coeff`'s index type, so cells, monomial exponents and label-multiplicity vectors are one type and no transport is needed between the sampling side and the generating-function side.

encoding_decisions.decision: All generating functions are FORMAL: `pgfSeries P : MvPowerSeries V ℝ := MvPowerSeries.mk (fun x => P.real {x})`, root clusters `rootCluster G α i : MvPowerSeries V ℝ`, and \(\Psi_P\) is the formal logarithm `PowerSeries.subst (pgfSeries P /ₚ p₀ - 1) (PowerSeries.log ℝ)`. No radius of convergence, no analyticity, no real-valued PGF evaluation anywhere.
encoding_decisions.why: Every proof in the frozen core is coefficient extraction from finite expressions; Mathlib supplies `PowerSeries.log`, `PowerSeries.subst` into an `MvPowerSeries` target, `PowerSeries.subst_exp_log`/`subst_log_exp_sub_one` for the exp/log inversion used in `thm:degree-four-completeness`, and `MvPowerSeries.coeff_pow` + `Finset.finsuppAntidiag` for the truncated log series used in `def:count-cell-map`. Working formally removes the only analytic obligation the paper never needed.

encoding_decisions.decision: Members of a DAG fiber are represented by their Boolean edge functions: `EdgeFn V := V → V → Bool` with `IsAcyclicEdgeFn`, and `edgeDAG e h : Causalean.DAG V := Causalean.DAG.ofAcyclic (fun u v => e u v = true) h`. Fibers are `Finset (EdgeFn V)`.
encoding_decisions.why: `Causalean.DAG` carries a `Decidable` instance as data, so two DAGs with the same edge relation are not definitionally equal; the cardinality claim \(|\mathcal D(P)|=\prod_T|T|\) in `prop:fiber-cardinality-certificates` needs a type with `DecidableEq`+`Fintype`. Boolean edge functions give that while `edgeDAG` keeps all Causalean DAG lemmas available.

encoding_decisions.decision: The undirected objects \(S(P)\) and \(F(P)\) are `SimpleGraph V`; \(\mathcal T_0(P)\) is a `Finset` of `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent` of \(F(P)\) and \(|T|\) is `(component.supp).ncard`.
encoding_decisions.why: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic`, `SimpleGraph.IsTree`, `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent` and `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic.isTree_connectedComponent` are exactly the forest/component vocabulary the source-forest theorem argues in.

encoding_decisions.decision: `oeq:polynomial-delay-inversion` is realized as a descriptive non-`Prop` payload (`_root_.String`), TWO-CASE rule case (B), never proved and never depended on.
encoding_decisions.why: The frozen node asks for termination 'with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\)'. The core fixes no machine model, no bit-length encoding of the inputs, and no definition of delay between successive output classes, and `def:outward-inversion-handle` is a prose recipe rather than a defined procedure; its obligation block states that a polynomial-delay conclusion cannot be derived honestly. Writing a `Prop` would require inventing a cost model the paper never fixes. The payload records every stated desideratum (exact output \(\mathcal D_n\), inclusion/exclusion certificates for every labeled DAG, polynomial delay in bit length and \(d\), preservation of the coverage conclusion), the stated obstruction and partial result, and the nonassertion disclaimer, so it changes whenever the question changes.

encoding_decisions.decision: Redirect revision: the non-`Prop` String transcribes only the frozen question's rational-input, exact-output, valid-certificate, polynomial-delay, and coverage desiderata, followed by a nonassertion disclaimer.
encoding_decisions.why: Polynomial checkability, obstruction, attempted-method, and partial-result narrative are not clauses of the frozen question and therefore are omitted from the payload.

encoding_decisions.decision: `thm:source-reversal` is stated with the two structural assumption atoms threaded directly (its frozen `depends_on` lists the atoms, not the class) plus explicit strictness binders `0 < μ i` and `α e ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1`.
encoding_decisions.why: `def:strict-pb-class` is not in this node's `depends_on`, so it may not appear in `hyps`; the strictness side conditions belong to the frozen class construction and are inlined as ordinary binders rather than introduced as new named assumptions.

encoding_decisions.decision: '\(P\) is generated by \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\)' is AMBIENT (S1), not a per-theorem hypothesis: S1's world is a strict PB-SCM together with its law. Where a frozen statement quantifies over a second law (`thm:degree-four-completeness`) the second law's strict-generation clause is expressed through the abbreviation `IsStrictLaw` over `StrictPBSCM`, and where it quantifies over a fiber member (`thm:local-signatures`, `thm:fixed-dag-decoder`, `thm:source-forest-fiber`) it is expressed as membership in / nonemptiness of `obsFiber P` (`def:observational-fiber`).
encoding_decisions.why: Keeps every statement's `hyps` a subset of its frozen `depends_on` without dropping the strictness content of the frozen statements.

encoding_decisions.decision: Redirect revision: genealogy weights inhabit `(0,1]`, encoded by `genealogyWeight_mem_Ioc`; all `@realizes \(w_\gamma\)` locations jointly carry the product formula and this range.
encoding_decisions.why: A sink-rooted genealogy has no outgoing edge trials, so its defining empty product equals 1.

substrate_survey.detail: `Causalean.DAG`, `DAG.parents`, `DAG.children`, `DAG.isRoot`, `DAG.roots`, `DAG.topoOrder`, `DAG.topoOrder_lt`, `DAG.descendants` — the labeled-DAG layer and the reverse-topological recursion principle. Scope of the reuse: the GRAPH COMPONENT of S1 only. The module carries a finite acyclic edge relation and graph operations; it hosts no innovation law, thinning array, structural recursion or observational law, so the S1 world itself is `define-local` (packaged by `StrictPBSCM`) rather than reused from this decl.
`Causalean.DAG.ofAcyclic` / `ofAcyclic_edge` materialize a DAG from a Boolean edge function plus an acyclicity proof (E4) and from the root-choice completion of `def:root-choice-family`.

The frozen source-edge condition (\(u\) a source and \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{u\}\)) implies `Causalean.DAG.IsCoveredEdge u v`, so the graph component of `def:source-reversal` is exactly `Causalean.DAG.flipEdge`, with `flipRel_acyclic` discharging the acyclicity half of `thm:source-reversal` and `flipEdge_edge` / `Causalean.SameSkeleton` giving the edge read-off and skeleton invariance.

`Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge` is the per-cell two-sided bounded-indicator tail bound used in `thm:coefficient-confidence`; the paper's hand-rolled tilting/Markov derivation is not rebuilt.

Markov equivalence is d-separation equivalence of DAGs; the present fiber is a strictly finer DISTRIBUTIONAL equivalence for a specific parametric count model (two DAGs in one PB-SCM fiber need not be Markov equivalent, and Markov-equivalent DAGs need not be in one fiber). Only `CoveredReversal` transfers, and it does (see above).

The cluster's identification substrate is about interventional functionals (backdoor/frontdoor/do-calculus/SWIG/potential outcomes) under a fixed known graph. This artifact identifies the GRAPH ITSELF from one observational count law and never forms an interventional distribution; there is no do-operator, no adjustment set and no treatment variable in the core. Nothing at that abstraction fits.

Recursive density factorization for finite-valued DAG models — measure-theoretic factorization of a joint density, not a generating-function/branching expansion; the PB-SCM law does not factor over the graph as a product of parent-conditional kernels of the observed counts in the form these files use.
Checked on the word 'forest': these are regression-tree / random-forest learners, not graph forests. The graph-forest vocabulary comes from Mathlib `SimpleGraph.Acyclic` instead.

Surveyed for a ready-made simultaneous multinomial-cell region. They give single-functional or empirical-Bernstein intervals; the frozen \(\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2|I_4|/\eta)/(2n)}\) is the plain Hoeffding-plus-union-bound radius, so the union bound over \(I_4\) is assembled inline on top of `hoeffding_abs_ge` rather than reusing a different radius.

env.world: A finite labeled vertex population \(V=[d]\) with \(d\ge2\), a labeled directed acyclic graph \(G\) on \(V\) with edge set \(E=E(G)\), parent and child maps \(\operatorname{Pa}_G,\operatorname{Ch}_G\), strictly positive innovation rates \(\mu\in(0,\infty)^V\) and strict edge thinning probabilities \(\alpha\in(0,1)^{E}\). Innovations \(\varepsilon_i\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\mu_i)\) and edge-and-individual trials \(B_{ijr}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\alpha_{ij})\) are mutually independent, the thinning operator is \(\alpha_{ij}\circ x=\sum_{r=1}^{x}B_{ijr}\), and the observed counts solve \(X_j=\varepsilon_j+\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Pa}_G(j)}\alpha_{ij}\circ X_i\), with observational law \(P=\mathcal L(X)\) on \(\mathbb N_0^V\). All generating functions are formal series in the indeterminates \(z=(z_v)_{v\in V}\): the root-cluster polynomials \(H_i\), the log probability-generating function \(\Psi_P\), its exact-support coefficients \(c_k\) and the degree-four signature \(t_4(P)\). No faithfulness, no edge-strength margin, no compact parameter box and no lower bound on \(p_0\) are imposed.
env.notes: WORLD DISPOSITION (corrected in round 2): `define-local`. No existing declaration packages this world. The local packaging is the `def:strict-pb-class` structure `StrictPBSCM G μ α P` (Basic.lean), which bundles the Poisson innovations, the Bernoulli thinning array, the structural recursion, the strictness clauses and the observational law \(P=\mathcal L(X)\); the strict-generation predicate is its abbreviation `IsStrictLaw`. `Causalean.DAG` is reused for the GRAPH COMPONENT ONLY (labeled DAG carrier, `parents`/`children`/`isRoot`/`topoOrder`/`descendants`), together with `Causalean.Graph.AcyclicConstruct.DAG.ofAcyclic` and `Causalean.Graph.MarkovEquiv.CoveredReversal.DAG.flipEdge` for graph construction and covered-edge reversal; it hosts no probabilistic or parametric content, so it cannot carry the S-block. World-level search trace (re-runnable): `grep -rE 'Poisson|thinning|branching|INAR|Galton' ../Causalean` → only `Stat/FiniteRaoBlackwell/PairedPoissonHistogram/*` (a paired-Poisson histogram risk calculation, no DAG/branching recursion) and no thinning operator; `grep -rE '^(structure|class) .*SCM' ../Causalean/SCM/Model` → `Causalean.SCM` / `Causalean.SCM.Model` generic structural-equation layers over arbitrary value spaces with no ℕ-valued additive thinning or innovation-law parameterization; Mathlib side `lean_leansearch "Poisson distribution probability mass function measure"` → `ProbabilityTheory.poissonPMF`/`poissonMeasure` (reused inside the local structure) and `"Bernoulli distribution PMF probability measure boolean"` → `PMF.bernoulli` (likewise); no bundled branching-process/PB-SCM world exists in either library. Encoding (process, not reader-facing): `V` is `[Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]` with `hd : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V`; `G : Causalean.DAG V` (../Causalean/Graph/DAG.lean); \(\operatorname{Pa}_G,\operatorname{Ch}_G\) are `DAG.parents`, `DAG.children`; sources are `DAG.isRoot`; reverse-topological recursion uses `DAG.topoOrder` + `DAG.topoOrder_lt` as the well-founded measure. \(\mu,\alpha\) are `V → ℝ` and `V → V → ℝ` with the strictness conditions imposed only on edges (E1). Counts and multi-indices are `Cell V := V →₀ ℕ` (E2). Series live in `MvPowerSeries V ℝ` (E3). Fiber members are Boolean edge functions (E4). \(S(P),F(P)\) are `SimpleGraph V` and \(\mathcal T_0(P)\) is a `Finset` of `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent` (E5). Ambient-hypothesis rule E8: being generated by \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\) is part of this world, not a per-node hypothesis.

env.world: Observational sampling from the law of S1: \(n\) independent draws \(X^{(1)},\dots,X^{(n)}\) of the complete labeled count vector from one fixed law \(P\) on \(\mathbb N_0^V\), a nominal error probability \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the finite low-count cell index \(I_4=\{x\in\mathbb N_0^V:|x|\le4\}\) with population cell probabilities \(p_x=P(X=x)\) and empirical frequencies \(\widehat p_x=n^{-1}\sum_{b\le n}\mathbf 1\{X^{(b)}=x\}\), the simultaneous radius \(\epsilon_n\), the truncated cell region \(Q_n\), the rational cell-to-coefficient map \(T\), the coefficient region \(C_n\), the outward-inverted graph set \(\mathcal D_n\) and the certified outward-inversion handle \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}\). There is no designated treatment and no overlap condition; in particular \(p_0\) is not bounded away from zero.
env.notes: Encoding: `S : Causalean.Stat.IIDSample Ω (Cell V) μ P` supplies `S.Z : ℕ → Ω → Cell V`, independence, identical distribution and `μ.map (S.Z 0) = P`; \(\widehat p_x\) is `S.sampleMean (fun y => if y = x then 1 else 0) n`, so `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge` applies verbatim with `a = 0`, `b = 1`. \(I_4\) is `Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Cell V => x.sum (fun _ m => m) ≤ 4)` (finite because `V` is finite). The union bound is Mathlib's `measure_biUnion_finset_le` over `I_4`.

ass:structural-recursion.notes: `def StructuralRecursion (G : Causalean.DAG V) (α : V → V → ℝ) (B : V → V → ℕ → Ω → Bool) (ε X : Ω → Cell V) : Prop := ∀ ω j, X ω j = ε ω j + ∑ i ∈ G.parents j, thin B i j (X ω i)` with `thin B i j x := ((Finset.range x).filter (fun r => B i j r ω)).card`, i.e. \(\alpha_{ij}\circ x=\sum_{r=1}^{x}B_{ijr}\). Modeling assumption (restriction on the data-generating mechanism) — threaded, never discharged. Search trace: grepped `../Causalean` for `thinning|branching|Poisson|INAR|binomial thin` (0 hits outside the unrelated `CausalSmith/Stat/.../PoissonInverseCount.lean`), surveyed `Causalean/SCM/Model/SCM.lean` + `Causalean/SCM/Model/Evaluation.lean` (generic structural-equation layer over arbitrary value types; it has no ℕ-valued additive-thinning recursion and wiring the count recursion through it would add an SCM evaluation obligation for no reuse); Mathlib side `lean_leansearch "Bernoulli distribution PMF probability measure boolean"` → `PMF.bernoulli` only (used for the marginal law in the companion atom, not for the recursion).

ass:independent-branching-law.notes: ADJUSTED IN F2: `def IndependentBranchingLaw (G) (μ α) (B ε) (P₀ : Measure Ω) : Prop` uses `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` for the common natural-valued encoding of innovations and Boolean trials, pins each innovation by the exact Poisson singleton-mass formula `exp (-μ_i) μ_i^n / n!`, and pins each edge trial by `P₀.real {B_ijr=true}=α_ij`. The pinned Mathlib checkout has an incompatible stale `Probability.Distributions.Poisson.olean` but no corresponding source file, so importing that leaf cannot compile; spelling the defining mass function is extensionally the same discrete law and uses targeted `Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exp`. Modeling assumption — threaded, never discharged. No product-of-Poisson-and-Bernoulli bundle exists, so the conjunction is assembled here.

ass:iid-sampling.notes: `def IidCountSampling (μΩ : Measure Ω) (P : Measure (Cell V)) (Z : ℕ → Ω → Cell V) : Prop := ∃ S : Causalean.Stat.IIDSample Ω (Cell V) μΩ P, S.Z = Z` — the Prop atom is a thin named wrapper whose whole content is the reused Causalean structure (independence + identical distribution + `μ.map (Z 0) = P`). Modeling/sampling assumption: threaded into `thm:coefficient-confidence`, never discharged.

def:strict-pb-class.notes: `structure StrictPBSCM (G : Causalean.DAG V) (μ : V → ℝ) (α : V → V → ℝ) (P : Measure (Cell V)) : Prop` with the two `by_member_properties` fields `recursion : ∃ Ω .. StructuralRecursion ..` and `branchingLaw : ∃ .. IndependentBranchingLaw ..` realized over a shared witness bundle, plus the frozen construction's side conditions as additional non-assumption fields `mu_pos : ∀ i, 0 < μ i`, `alpha_strict : ∀ i j, G.edge i j → α i j ∈ Set.Ioo (0:ℝ) 1`, and `law : P = Measure.map X P₀` (\(P=\mathcal L(X)\)). Only the two listed members are assumption atoms; the strictness/law fields are the frozen construction's own clauses, not new assumptions. Derived abbreviation `IsStrictLaw P : Prop := ∃ G μ α, StrictPBSCM G μ α P` (E8). Search trace: surveyed `Causalean/SCM/Model/SCM.lean`, `Causalean/SCM/Model/Kernel.lean`, `Causalean/SCM/Factored/*` for a parametric count-model class — all are generic SCMs over arbitrary value spaces with no Poisson/thinning parameterization; `lean_local_search "Poisson"` returns one unrelated CausalSmith helper. No fit.

def:root-cluster.notes: `noncomputable def rootCluster (G) (α) : V → MvPowerSeries V ℝ` by well-founded recursion on `G.topoOrder` (decreasing along `G.children` via `DAG.topoOrder_lt`): `rootCluster i = MvPowerSeries.X i * ∏ j ∈ G.children i, (C (1 - α i j) + C (α i j) * rootCluster j)`; companion `logPGFPoly G μ α : MvPowerSeries V ℝ := ∑ i, C (μ i) * (rootCluster i - 1)` for \(\Psi_P\). Each `rootCluster i` is in fact a polynomial (finite support) — recorded as a helper lemma, not a separate node. Search trace: `lean_local_search "GeneratingFunction"` → empty; `lean_leansearch "probability generating function of a discrete random variable"` → only `mgf`/`cgf` (real-variable moment/cumulant generating functions, wrong object); no branching-process or Galton–Watson substrate in Mathlib or `../Causalean` (grepped `branching`, `Galton`, `pgf`). Build-inline over Mathlib `MvPowerSeries`.

def:log-pgf-coordinates.notes: `pgfSeries P : MvPowerSeries V ℝ := MvPowerSeries.mk (fun x => P.real {x})`; for `p₀ := P.real {0} > 0`, `logPGFSeries P := PowerSeries.subst ((p₀)⁻¹ • pgfSeries P - 1) (PowerSeries.log ℝ)` (legal since the argument has zero constant coefficient, `PowerSeries.HasSubst`); `logPGFCoeff P k := MvPowerSeries.coeff k (logPGFSeries P)` = \(c_k\) for \(k\ne0\) (the subtraction of \(\Psi_P(0)\) is exactly the normalization by \(p_0\)); `signature4 P : {k // 1 ≤ |k| ≤ 4} → ℝ` = \(t_4(P)\). Search trace: `lean_loogle "PowerSeries.log"` → `PowerSeries.log`, `PowerSeries.logOf_eq`, `PowerSeries.subst_exp_log`, `PowerSeries.subst_log_exp_sub_one` (all reused); `lean_loogle "PowerSeries.subst"` confirms `PowerSeries.subst : MvPowerSeries τ S → PowerSeries R → MvPowerSeries τ S`, so the univariate formal logarithm substitutes into the multivariate series directly and no multivariate `log` needs to be built. `lean_leansearch "multivariate power series coefficient exp log formal"` → no `MvPowerSeries.log`.

def:genealogy-expansion.notes: ADJUSTED IN F2: `Genealogy G i` is a structure whose finite `paths : Finset (List V)` are prefix-closed, start at `i`, and follow `G.edge`; occurrence paths retain repeated labels reached by distinct downstream routes. `Genealogy.multiplicity` sums the last label of every occurrence path, and `genealogyWeight` multiplies the open/closed Bernoulli factor for each outgoing edge at every occurrence. `genealogiesWith` filters the finite valid genealogy space at multiplicity `k`; finiteness follows from DAG acyclicity. The planned directly nested indexed `Option (Genealogy G j)` constructor is rejected by Lean's kernel because nested inductive parameters may not contain the local index `j`. This path-set representation is definitionally explicit and mathematically equivalent to the frozen finite open-edge genealogy. Search trace and build-inline disposition are unchanged.

def:observational-fiber.notes: `noncomputable def obsFiber (P : Measure (Cell V)) : Finset (EdgeFn V) := Finset.univ.filter (fun e => ∃ (h : IsAcyclicEdgeFn e) (μ α), StrictPBSCM (edgeDAG e h) μ α P)` (classical decidability), realizing \(\mathcal D(P)=\{G':\exists(\mu',\alpha')\ (G',\mu',\alpha',P)\in\mathcal M_d^\circ\}\) under E4. Search trace: `../doc/API.md` §9 `SCM/ID/Identifiable.lean` and §9b were read for an existing observational-equivalence-class object; `Causalean.Identifiable` is 'two SCMs agreeing on the observational law agree on an interventional functional' — a different (functional-level) object with no graph fiber; `Causalean/Graph/MarkovEquiv/Defs.lean` `MarkovEquiv` is d-separation equivalence, coarser and distinct (bypass-justified above). No fit.

def:signature-skeleton.notes: `noncomputable def sigSkeleton (P) : SimpleGraph V` with `Adj i j := i ≠ j ∧ 0 < logPGFCoeff P (e i + e j)`, symmetric by construction. Small node — reuse check done anyway: Mathlib `SimpleGraph` is the carrier (reused as the ambient type); no library predicate reads a skeleton off generating-function coefficients. Search trace: grepped `../Causalean` for `skeleton` → `Causalean.SameSkeleton` / `DAG.UAdj` (`Graph/MarkovEquiv/Defs.lean`), which compare two DAGs' adjacency rather than construct one from a law; `Causalean.DAG.UAdj` will be reused inside `thm:local-signatures` to state that `sigSkeleton` equals the undirected adjacency of any fiber member.

def:signature-heads.notes: `def SigHead (P) (i j k : V) : Prop := (i ≠ j ∧ i ≠ k ∧ j ≠ k) ∧ 0 < c (e i + e k) * c (e j + e k) ∧ ((c (e i + e j) = 0 ∧ c (e i + e j + e k) = 0) ∨ (0 < c (e i + e j) ∧ 0 < c (e i + e j + 2 • e k)))`, transcribing \(\mathsf{Head}_P\) clause for clause. Search trace: grepped `../Causalean` for `collider|immorality` → `Causalean.DAG.IsImmorality` (`Graph/MarkovEquiv/Defs.lean`) is a GRAPH predicate (two nonadjacent parents of a common child); it is reused on the graph side of `thm:local-signatures` but cannot define the law-side predicate, which is what this node is.

def:signature-residual.notes: Three companion defs in one file: `compelledArrows P : Finset (V × V)` = \(A(P)=\{i\to k:\exists j,\ \mathsf{Head}_P(i,j;k)\}\), `multiParents P : Finset V` = \(M(P)\), and `residualGraph P : SimpleGraph V` = \(F(P)=S(P)\setminus\{\{i,k\}:i\to k\in A(P)\}\) (as `sigSkeleton P \ (fromEdgeSet of the compelled pairs)`). lean_name names the first; all three are this node. Small/derived — no library analogue (they are functionals of this paper's signature predicates); survey as for `def:signature-heads`.

def:root-choice-family.notes: `freeComponents P : Finset ((residualGraph P).ConnectedComponent)` = \(\mathcal T_0(P)\) (components disjoint from `multiParents P`), and `rootChoiceCompletion P ρ : EdgeFn V` = \(G_\rho\): the compelled arrows together with, in each component, the orientation away from the anchor \(m\) (if the component meets \(M(P)\)) or away from \(\rho(T)\) (if free), 'away from \(r\)' being 'the unique residual path from \(r\) reaches the tail before the head'. Reuses Mathlib `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent`, `ConnectedComponent.supp`, `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic.isTree_connectedComponent`, `SimpleGraph.Walk`/`Path` uniqueness on trees for the orientation, and `Causalean.DAG.ofAcyclic` to materialize the completion as a DAG. Search trace: `lean_leansearch "simple graph is acyclic forest connected component tree"` → `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic`, `IsTree`, `IsAcyclic.isTree_connectedComponent`, `isTree_iff` (all reused); grepped `../Causalean` for `Forest|connectedComponent|IsTree` → only `ML/Tree/Forest.lean` (random forests, unrelated). No orientation-away-from-a-root construction exists upstream; build-inline.

def:source-reversal.notes: Graph component REUSED: under the frozen side condition (`G.isRoot u`, `G.parents v = {u}`, `G.edge u v`) one proves `hcov : Causalean.DAG.IsCoveredEdge G u v` in two lines (`IsCoveredEdge u v := G.edge u v ∧ ∀ c ≠ u, (G.edge c u ↔ G.edge c v)`; both sides are false for `c ≠ u` because `u` is a source and `v`'s only parent is `u`), and the reversed graph is `Causalean.DAG.flipEdge hcov`, whose acyclicity is `Causalean.DAG.flipRel_acyclic` and whose edges are read off by `Causalean.DAG.flipEdge_edge`. Only the parameter component is new: `sourceReversal G μ α u v : (V → ℝ) × (V → V → ℝ)` with \(\mu'_u=\mu_u(1-\alpha_{uv})\), \(\mu'_v=\mu_v+\mu_u\alpha_{uv}\), \(\alpha'_{vu}=\mu_u\alpha_{uv}/(\mu_v+\mu_u\alpha_{uv})\), all else unchanged. Disposition is `define-local` because the node is the whole triple map, not the graph map alone; the internal reuse is recorded here so 2.5 sees a justified, non-bypassing use of the cluster substrate.

def:rational-decoder.notes: `noncomputable def decodeBeta (G) (c) : V → ℝ` and `decodeAlpha`, mutually defined by well-founded recursion on `G.topoOrder` in DECREASING order (children first, via `DAG.topoOrder_lt`): `decodeAlpha i j = c (e i + e j) / (c (e i + e j) + c (e i) * decodeBeta j)`, `decodeBeta i = ∏ j ∈ G.children i, (1 - decodeAlpha i j)`, `decodeMu i = c (e i) / decodeBeta i`; `decodeParams G P := (decodeMu, decodeAlpha)` = \(\theta_G(P)\). Search trace: grepped `../Causalean` for `topological order recursion` helpers → `DAG.topoOrder`/`topoOrder_lt`/`isAncestor_topoOrder_lt` (reused as the termination measure); Mathlib side `lean_leansearch` for reverse-topological recursion on a DAG returns nothing structural to reuse. Build-inline.

def:triangle-witness.notes: `def triangleWitness (r : V) (s m : V) : Causalean.DAG V × (V → ℝ) × (V → V → ℝ)` on the transitive triangle \(s\to m\to r,\ s\to r\) with \(\mu_s=6,\mu_m=2,\mu_r=1\), \(\alpha_{sm}=2/3,\alpha_{sr}=\alpha_{mr}=1/2\) and every other vertex isolated with its own positive rate (the \(d>3\) extension of the frozen witness). Built with `Causalean.DAG.ofAcyclic`. Concrete numeric witness — nothing to reuse; survey recorded under `def:strict-pb-class` (no parametric count-model examples exist in `Causalean/SCM/Examples/*`, which are linear-Gaussian / binary backdoor and IV DAGs).

def:count-cell-map.notes: `def lowCells : Finset (Cell V) := Finset.univ.filter (fun x => x.sum (fun _ m => m) ≤ 4)` = \(I_4\) and `def cellToCoeff (q : Cell V → ℝ) (k : Cell V) : ℝ := ∑ ℓ ∈ Finset.Icc 1 |k|, ((-1)^(ℓ+1)/ℓ) * ∑ t ∈ (Finset.range ℓ).finsuppAntidiag k |>.filter (fun t => ∀ a, t a ≠ 0), ∏ a ∈ Finset.range ℓ, q (t a) / q 0` = \(T_k(q)\), the ORDERED-tuple sum of the frozen definition. Search trace: `Finset.finsuppAntidiag` is the ordered multi-index decomposition Mathlib already uses in `MvPowerSeries.coeff_pow` (`lean_leansearch "multivariate power series coefficient exp log formal"`); no truncated-log-coefficient functional exists upstream, so the finite sum is written out here and connected to `logPGFCoeff` by `thm:coefficient-confidence`.

def:coefficient-region.notes: `cellRadius n η : ℝ := Real.sqrt (Real.log (2 * lowCells.card / η) / (2 * n))` = \(\epsilon_n\); `cellRegion n η p̂ : Set (Cell V → ℝ)` = \(Q_n\) (nonnegativity, truncated mass ≤ 1, \(q_0>0\), and the simultaneous interval constraints); `coeffRegion n η p̂ : Set (Cell V → ℝ) := cellToCoeff '' cellRegion …` = \(C_n\). Empirical frequencies \(\widehat p_x\) come from the reused `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.sampleMean` of the cell indicator (S2). Search trace: surveyed `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/UniformDeviation/ConfidenceInterval.lean` and `TailBounds/{Bernstein,EmpiricalBernstein}.lean` for a ready-made simultaneous cell region — none has the frozen Hoeffding+union radius; recorded as bypass-justified above.

def:outer-fiber.notes: `fiberAtSignature (t : Cell V → ℝ) : Finset (EdgeFn V)` = \(\mathcal D(t)=\{G:\exists(G,\mu,\alpha,P')\in\mathcal M_d^\circ,\ t_4(P')=t\}\), and `outerFiber n η p̂ : Finset (EdgeFn V) := (coeffRegion …).biUnion-as-filter`, i.e. `Finset.univ.filter (fun e => ∃ t ∈ coeffRegion …, e ∈ fiberAtSignature t)` (a `Finset` because `EdgeFn V` is a `Fintype`, even though the union is over a continuum of \(t\)). Same survey as `def:observational-fiber`: no library object for a law-indexed graph fiber.

def:outward-inversion-handle.redirect_revision: `OutwardInversionCertificate` now proves interval enclosures over the full coefficient region, exact source-forest enumeration semantics, a genuine reverse-topological order, valid rate and edge-parameter interval decoding, and a monotone branch-and-bound trace that preserves the target and finishes at the output. `IsOutwardInversionHandle` couples these certificates to exact inclusion/exclusion verdicts.
def:outward-inversion-handle.notes: `def IsOutwardInversionHandle (A : ℕ → ℚ → (Cell V → ℚ) → List (EdgeFn V)) : Prop := ∀ n η p̂, (A n η p̂).Nodup ∧ (A n η p̂).toFinset = outerFiber n η p̂ ∧ ∀ e : EdgeFn V, (e ∈ A n η p̂ ↔ e ∈ outerFiber n η p̂)` — the two truth-valued clauses the frozen handle states (exact recovery of the target set \(\mathcal D_n\); a decided inclusion/exclusion verdict for every labeled DAG). Search trace (re-runnable) establishing that no existing handle/specification abstraction fits. Causalean: `grep -rE '^(structure|def|abbrev|class) \w*(Spec|Correct|Enumerat|Handle|Algorithm)\w*' ../Causalean` → three hits, `Estimation/NPIV/Operator/SpectralCalculus.lean:116 SpectralSourceCondition` (a spectral smoothness condition, unrelated), `Experimentation/DesignBased/PotentialOutcome.lean:43 ProperlySpecified` (a potential-outcome consistency predicate, unrelated), and the only genuine algorithm-specification analogue `Causalean.SCM.ID.idAlgorithm` (`../Causalean/SCM/ID/DiscreteID/Checker.lean:138`) with its soundness theorem `idAlgorithm_success_toRec` (:152); `grep -rE 'IsAlgorithm|Enumerat|Certificate|PolynomialDelay|OpenQuestion' ../Causalean` → certificate hits are all interval-enclosure checkers (`Mathlib/Probability/CertifiedFiniteMarkovExpectation/**`), no set-enumeration specification. ANALOGOUS MODULE, not a fit: `idAlgorithm` is a fuel-bounded Boolean checker for Tian–Shpitser identifiability of ONE query on a `SWIGGraph`, specified by a one-directional soundness implication into `idSucceedsRec`; it is neither a generic 'procedure meets its set-valued specification' abstraction nor over this artifact's `EdgeFn V`/`outerFiber` objects, and it carries no exactness (`toFinset = target`) or per-object inclusion/exclusion clause. F3 may nevertheless imitate its checker-plus-soundness-theorem shape. Mathlib: `lean_leansearch "algorithm enumerates a set with polynomial delay complexity certificate"` → `Set.enumerate`, `Set.enumerateCountable` (+ their membership/range lemmas) and `Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith.CertificateOracle` — selection-function enumerations of a set and a linarith oracle, none of which carry an exact-output, certificate, or complexity specification; Mathlib has no complexity-theoretic layer at all. Hence `define-local`. NO TAUTOLOGICAL CONJUNCTS: the frozen construction's procedural recipe (interval screening, source-forest component enumeration, reverse-topological interval decoding, certificate-preserving branch-and-bound) is a description of HOW a handle would be built, not a truth condition the core defines, so it is deliberately left out of the Prop and recorded here as presentation-only narrative. Consumed only by `oeq:polynomial-delay-inversion`.

lem:genealogy-coefficient.notes: `theorem logPGFCoeff_eq_genealogy_sum (h : StrictPBSCM G μ α P) {k : Cell V} (hk : k ≠ 0) : logPGFCoeff P k = ∑ i, μ i * ∑ γ ∈ genealogiesWith G α i k, genealogyWeight α γ`. Proof chain planned in three helper lemmas inside the same file: (i) `rootCluster_eq_occurrence_pgf` — reverse-topological induction giving `MvPowerSeries.coeff k (rootCluster G α i) = ∑ γ ∈ genealogiesWith G α i k, genealogyWeight α γ` (pure formal algebra + the `Genealogy` Fintype); (ii) the compound-Poisson bridge `logPGFSeries P = logPGFPoly G μ α`, i.e. a Poisson(μ_i) number of i.i.d. clusters with cluster series `rootCluster i` superposed independently across `i` has formal PGF `exp(∑ μ_i (H_i - 1))` — this is the one genuinely measure-theoretic step, built from `ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure`, independence of the innovation/trial family, and `PowerSeries.subst_exp_log`/`PowerSeries.subst_log_exp_sub_one` for the log/exp inversion; (iii) coefficient extraction, with positivity of every weight from strictness. Paper-owned (`status: proved`) ⇒ IN SCOPE, `defer_tier:false`, `gate:false` regardless of the size of step (ii). Search trace for (ii): `lean_leansearch "probability generating function of a discrete random variable"` → only `mgf`/`cgf`; grepped `../Causalean` for `branching|Galton|compound Poisson|thinning` → no hits; `../doc/API.md` §10z (minimax/nonparametric substrate) and §Stat/ were scanned for a generating-function layer — absent. ANALOGOUS MODULE for the induction pattern: `Causalean/SCM/Factored/*.lean` (recursive Markov factorization of `jointKernel` by reverse-topological induction over `DAG.topoOrder`) — F3 should adapt its induction skeleton; the gap to bridge is that the factored files induct on conditional kernels while this file inducts on formal series coefficients.

thm:local-signatures.notes: Four conclusions in one theorem (with the exact-support pair identity \(c_{e_i+e_j}=c_{e_i}\alpha_{ij}\beta_j/(1-\alpha_{ij})\) factored out as a reusable helper lemma for `thm:fixed-dag-decoder`): pair-coefficient positivity ⇔ skeleton adjacency (stated against `Causalean.DAG.UAdj` of any fiber member); the induced-path degree-three vanishing criterion; the triangle degree-four criterion; and `compelledArrows P` = the arrows entering indegree-≥2 vertices in every member of `obsFiber P`. Strictness is ambient (S1/E8) and the fiber quantification uses `def:observational-fiber` ∈ `depends_on`, so `hyps` is empty. Reuses `Causalean.DAG.IsImmorality`/`UAdj` on the graph side. Paper-owned, in scope.

thm:source-reversal.notes: Three conclusions: acyclicity and strictness of the transformed system, and the COMPLETE formal identity `logPGFPoly (flipEdge hcov) μ' α' = logPGFPoly G μ α` including the constant coefficient, with no disjointness assumption on the descendant sets of \(u\) and \(v\). Acyclicity is discharged by the reused `Causalean.DAG.flipRel_acyclic` via the `IsCoveredEdge` derivation recorded under `def:source-reversal`; the identity is the frozen four-line polynomial computation `μ_u U(1-t+tW) + μ_v W = μ'_u U + μ'_v W(1-s+sU)` plus `μ'_u + μ'_v = μ_u + μ_v`. The two frozen assumption atoms are threaded directly (E7); the strictness binders `0 < μ i`, `α e ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1` are inlined side conditions from the frozen class construction, not new assumptions.

thm:fixed-dag-decoder.redirect_revision: The theorem signature explicitly includes `hd : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V`, matching the frozen domain d ∈ {2,3,…}.
thm:fixed-dag-decoder.notes: For `e ∈ obsFiber P`: (a) `decodeParams (edgeDAG e h) P` returns a strict parameter point inducing \(P\); (b) it is the UNIQUE such point; (c) every denominator is positive; (d) the fixed-DAG coefficient map has full column rank \(d+m\) throughout \((0,\infty)^V\times(0,1)^{E(G)}\). (d) is proved exactly as in the frozen proof: differentiate the left-inverse identity \(R_G\circ\pi\Phi_G=\mathrm{id}\) and read off injectivity of the differential — Mathlib `fderiv_comp` / `HasFDerivAt.comp` plus `LinearMap.rank`-style injectivity; no rank machinery beyond a left inverse is needed. Paper-owned, in scope, `hyps` empty (fiber membership is a `def:observational-fiber` dependency).

thm:source-forest-fiber.notes: The kernel theorem: `(obsFiber P).Nonempty → ((residualGraph P).IsAcyclic ∧ (∀ T : (residualGraph P).ConnectedComponent, (T.supp ∩ multiParents P).Subsingleton) ∧ obsFiber P = Finset.image (rootChoiceCompletion P) {ρ | ∀ T ∈ freeComponents P, ρ T ∈ T.supp})`, together with the two orientation clauses (anchored components directed away from their unique anchor, free components away from the chosen root). Necessity is the residual-indegree/topological-order argument; sufficiency is the finite chain of reused `Causalean.DAG.flipEdge` steps along the unique tree path, each step licensed by `thm:source-reversal`. Reuses Mathlib `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic`, `IsAcyclic.isTree_connectedComponent`, walk/path uniqueness on trees. Paper-owned, in scope.

prop:fiber-cardinality-certificates.redirect_revision: The anchor certificate is a simple nonbacktracking path with uniqueness among all simple anchor-to-head walks. Reversal certificates are lists of strict parameter states over the fixed law P; each adjacent state is exactly the graph/rate/thinning image of `sourceReversal`, so the maps compose while preserving P and strictness.
prop:fiber-cardinality-certificates.notes: `(obsFiber P).card = ∏ T ∈ freeComponents P, T.supp.card` (injectivity+surjectivity of the root-choice map, the root being the unique residual-indegree-zero vertex), plus the compelled/reversible dichotomy: an edge is compelled iff it does not lie in a free tree, with the two certificate forms (a local head signature, or the unique path from an anchor) and, for a free-tree edge, both orientations realized by an explicit finite sequence of `sourceReversal` steps. `prop:` maps to `lean_kind:"theorem"` per the node→Lean rule. Paper-owned, in scope.

thm:degree-four-completeness.notes: `IsStrictLaw P → IsStrictLaw P' → (signature4 P = signature4 P' ↔ P = P')`, plus `obsFiber P = obsFiber P'` and `decodeParams G P = decodeParams G P'` for every common fiber member. The 'exponentiate the equal log-PGFs' step is Mathlib's formal inversion `PowerSeries.subst_exp_log` / `PowerSeries.subst_log_exp_sub_one`, after which `MvPowerSeries.ext` on cell coefficients gives `P = P'` via `Measure.ext_of_singleton`-style extensionality on the countable discrete `Cell V`. E8: the 'generated by \(\mathcal M_d^\circ\)' clause of the frozen statement is carried by `IsStrictLaw` (an abbreviation over the `def:strict-pb-class` structure); `def:strict-pb-class` is NOT in this node's frozen `depends_on`, so it is deliberately absent from `hyps` rather than dropped from the Lean statement. Paper-owned, in scope.

thm:degree-three-sharpness.redirect_revision: The constant-coefficient clauses assert equality of the three values. They do not assert the dimension-three-only value -9; with isolated rate-one extensions the common value is -(Fintype.card V + 6).
thm:degree-three-sharpness.notes: For the three sink choices \(r\) in `triangleWitness`: identical \(\Psi^{(r)}(0)=-9\), identical \(c_k\) for all \(|k|\le3\), differing coefficient of \(z_sz_mz_r^2\), and `obsFiber P^{(r)}` having pairwise different triangle sinks; the \(d>3\) extension by appending independent positive-Poisson coordinates. Everything is explicit polynomial arithmetic in `MvPowerSeries V ℝ` plus the adjacency criterion (5) of the frozen proof, which is the pair-coefficient helper factored out of `thm:local-signatures`. `def:strict-pb-class` in `depends_on` is USED (the witnesses are proved to be strict models), not assumed ⇒ `hyps` empty. Paper-owned, in scope.

thm:coefficient-confidence.notes: Two conclusions: (a) the exact finite rational identity `cellToCoeff (fun x => P.real {x}) k = logPGFCoeff P k` for `1 ≤ |k| ≤ 4` whenever `0 < p₀` (formal truncated log series; only \(\ell\le|k|\) and \(|x_a|\le4\) contribute, so no higher cell is involved); (b) `μΩ.real {ω | signature4 P ∈ coeffRegion n η (p̂ ω)} ≥ 1 - η`, finite-sample and uniform over the strict class with NO lower bound on \(p_0\). Step (b) REUSES `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge` per cell (indicator of `{x}`, `a = 0`, `b = 1`, giving `2 exp(-2 n ε²)`) and closes with Mathlib's finite union bound `measure_biUnion_finset_le` over `lowCells`; the frozen proof's hand-rolled exponential-tilting derivation is therefore NOT rebuilt. Paper-owned, in scope.

thm:outer-fiber-confidence.notes: `μΩ.real {ω | obsFiber P ⊆ outerFiber n η (p̂ ω)} ≥ 1 - η` uniformly over the strict class, plus the unanimity reporting rule: if the rule outputs nothing when `outerFiber = ∅` and otherwise only arrows with the same orientation in every member of `outerFiber`, the UNCONDITIONAL probability of reporting an arrow not compelled throughout `obsFiber P` is at most \(\eta\) (the frozen proof's event inclusion; no division by `Pr{D_n ≠ ∅}`). `ass:iid-sampling` is NOT in this node's frozen `depends_on`, so it is absent from `hyps`: the sampling structure is ambient (S2, `binds_sampling_model: true`) and the coverage event is imported from `thm:coefficient-confidence`, which is in `depends_on`. Paper-owned, in scope.
